methodological_rigor.justification: The study employs multiple complementary mouse models (SmoM2, Gnas-eKO, PKI), genetic epistasis experiments (double knockouts), bulk and single-cell RNA-seq, in vitro reporter assays, in vivo two-photon microscopy, and human BCC mutation analysis. Randomization is described for drug treatment groups, both sexes are included, and littermate controls are used throughout. Sample sizes are modest (N=3-15 per group) but appropriate for the study type; statistical analysis uses appropriate tests (Welch t-test, ANOVA with post-hoc, Wilcoxon) with combination synergy analysis. The lack of formal power calculations and investigator non-blinding to treatment allocation are minor limitations.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: This is a preclinical mechanistic study in mouse BCC models with human mutation validation. Oxford LoE is 5. Clinical relevance is moderate: BCC is the most common human cancer, the study identifies a potentially targetable pathway (ADORA2B activation with BAY60-6583), and mutation analysis in human tumors supports translational relevance. However, BAY60-6583 is not an approved drug, and the BCC mouse models have acknowledged limitations regarding mutational burden and model fidelity.

reporting_quality.justification: Animal experiments are well-reported with sample sizes, both sexes included, randomization described, and statistical tests specified per figure legend. Cell line authentication, mycoplasma testing, and RRID codes are provided. Primers and antibodies are in supplementary tables. No formal statement on raw sequencing data deposition is present in the main text, though the study mentions CCR Single Cell Analysis and Sequencing Facilities for data generation. No data sharing statement or repository accession numbers are visible.

novelty_literature.justification: The study provides the first comprehensive comparison of canonical (SmoM2) and non-canonical (Gαs/PKA inactivation) BCC models at the single-cell level, demonstrating near-identical tumor phenotypes. The finding that Gαs/PKA-driven tumors are SMO-independent and vismodegib-resistant is an important mechanistic insight. The therapeutic proof-of-concept for ADORA2B agonism is novel, though the concept of cAMP elevation as a Hedgehog inhibitor has been partially explored. The identification of PKA-inactivating mutations in human BCC adds a clinically relevant dimension.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is logically structured, moving from comparative tumor characterization through mechanistic analysis to therapeutic validation. Figure legends are detailed and informative. The discussion clearly acknowledges model limitations. The text is generally precise with good use of quantitative data. Minor issues include the density of mouse model acronyms which can make sections harder to follow for non-specialist readers.

key_strengths: Comprehensive multi-model comparison using bulk RNA-seq, scRNA-seq, and histology establishing near-equivalence of canonical and non-canonical BCC pathways
Genetic epistasis demonstrating SMO-independence of Gαs/PKA-driven tumors, with vismodegib resistance validation
Human BCC mutation analysis linking PKA-inactivating variants to functional impairment of GLI phosphorylation
In vivo therapeutic proof-of-concept for ADORA2B agonism as an alternative to SMO inhibitors in drug-resistant BCC
key_concerns: SmoM2 model represents basaloid follicular hamartoma rather than true BCC, partially undermining therapeutic relevance claims
BAY60-6583 in vivo efficacy tested only with topical 10-day treatment in a single mouse model; no pharmacokinetics or dose-response data provided
Small sample sizes for scRNA-seq (N=2 mice per genotype) limit statistical power for cell population inference
No raw sequencing data deposition accession numbers provided, limiting reproducibility
chief_reviewer.rationale: This mechanistically rigorous study advances understanding of BCC pathogenesis by establishing the equivalence of canonical and non-canonical Hedgehog activation and identifying a novel therapeutic strategy. The SMO-independent, vismodegib-resistant model with human mutation validation and in vivo therapeutic proof-of-concept meets Tier 2 standards, with minor revisions needed to address model limitations and data availability.
